sdf_offset — 3D sdf_csg op

• Data kinds: sdf → sdf

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sdf_offset(sdf, r) (to call the implementation directly, import sdf_ops; sdf_ops.sdf_offset(sdf, r); from the registry, ops3d.get("sdf_offset"))

Usage

Move an SDF's zero level set by a distance r along the normal = sdf − r (r>0 inflates, r<0 shrinks).

The new zero set is the isosurface sdf == r of the old field. The distance shifts uniformly by r at every point, so its properties as a distance field (gradient norm 1) are preserved. Used to give primitives thickness (rounded shells) or to secure clearance for piping.

Computation: np.asarray(sdf, float64) - float(r). r must be a scalar (passing an array gives TypeError from float()). The unit is the distance unit of sdf. r = 0 is the identity. No checks on shape, NaN or inf (inf - r = inf propagates as per the contract).

Geometric meaning: for an exact SDF it equals the Minkowski sum (r > 0 dilates by a sphere of radius r, r < 0 erodes). Applying r to sphere_sdf(g, c, R) gives exactly sphere_sdf(g, c, R + r). Dilating box_sdf rounds the corners (as it is a Euclidean dilation, the box does not just get bigger but becomes a rounded box with corner R = r).

Notes:

• When eroding (r < 0), if |r| exceeds the smallest inscribed radius the shape vanishes (every element positive). This is not an error.

• The inside of sdf_union / sdf_intersect is a lower bound of the true distance, so eroding with r < 0 after combining can remove more than it should in the overlap region.

• Shell of thickness t: sdf_subtract(sdf, sdf_offset(sdf, -t)).
